blocks.p: The *Radio* tab of the *Character* window gives each set a face of its own: the two radios, the hand-built radio and the CD player.

caption: Figure 57-1
The hand-built radio, left, and the CD player, right.

blocks.p: The hand-built radio is drawn as the board you wired. Its screen gives the band, the frequency and the station.
The CD player's screen reads *NO DISC* when it holds no disc. To change its battery, click the battery meter on the screen.

marks.text: The hand-built radio is the board you wired. The rocker turns it on.
Click the battery meter on the screen to change the battery.

sticky.text: Each set has its own face in the Radio tab.

blocks.p: The two radios are worked from their faces as the sets are: *PWR* turns the set on, *VOL* sets the volume and *TUNE* tunes it. To store a station, hold a preset key; press the key to tune back to the station.

caption: Figure 57-2
The Premium radio, left, and the ValuTech radio, right.

blocks.p: The Premium radio also takes a disc you carry, in the slot along its top. The eject key gives the disc back. Both radios show the battery at *BATT*.
The ValuTech radio has no disc slot; a dial scale runs across its top.

marks.text: The Premium radio takes a disc you carry in its slot. The eject key gives it back.
PWR, VOL and TUNE work as on the set.
A preset key held stores the station; pressed, it tunes back to it.

sticky.text: Two radios, worked as the sets are.
